name: Magnet
description: An element that leans towards the cursor before the cursor arrives

notes: No canvas and no WebGL. One CSS transform
Reads the pointer at window scope, because the point is reacting to a cursor that is still outside the element
The easing is a CSS transition rather than a per-frame spring, so nothing integrates and renderAtTime stays pure
One getBoundingClientRect per frame while the cursor is in range, and none when it is not

reach.description: How far outside the element the pull starts, as a multiple of its own size. 1 is one element-width of empty space around it. Large values on a small button make it twitch at things happening on the other side of the page.

strength.description: How far the element travels towards the cursor, as a fraction of the gap. Above 0.6 the cursor can never catch it, which is funny once and annoying afterwards.

maxShift.description: Cap on the travel, whatever the strength works out to. This is what stops a wide element sliding out of its own layout.

scale.description: Scale at full pull. 1 is no growth.

rotate.description: Degrees of lean at full pull, following the cursor left and right. Off by default: on text it reads as a wobble rather than a lean.

ease.description: How long it takes to follow the cursor, and to let go. Low is a rubber band; high is treacle. The release matters more than the catch.

reducedMotionTime.description: The single frame shown when the user prefers reduced motion. At rest there is no pointer, so this draws the element unmoved, which is the right answer.

instruction: move the cursor near the button, not onto it
